analysis: Balanced multi-negative BCE succeeded in this trial: host validation macro HR@10 was 0.5387 versus the reported previous ConvRec result of 0.4987, an absolute gain of 0.0400. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.575, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.585, Electronics 0.365, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.630. Electronics improved only slightly from the reported 0.360 and remained below the reported SASRec baseline of 0.420. The result supports balanced BCE for this configuration, but does not establish the mechanism or consistency across seeds. BCE independently supervises positive and negative scores with equal aggregate weight per position; target collisions are excluded and the negative term is normalized by its allowed count. No test metrics were supplied.
code_summary: One independent ConvRec model per category: 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, jointly learned item bias, four residual causal convolution blocks with dilations 1/2/4/8, LayerNorm, GELU, dropout 0.25, and sequence length 64. Training uses balanced BCE with 256 shared uniform negatives drawn with replacement and up to 2048 uniformly sampled target positions. AdamW, batch size 128, 200 steps per epoch, environment-controlled 200-epoch default, and 35-epoch early stopping are preserved. Each category selects and reloads exactly one validation-best checkpoint; the generated predictor reconstructs the same architecture and routes requests by dataset. No ensembles or separately fitted scoring components are used.
